reason: The disposition is right: no slot or build on 28-29 Sep, and a user OK is needed by name. That follows from R8, the v3/v4 W3/W4 tables (a new lever is not an allowed row), no honest lab and unmeasured runtime. The finding's NEW VERDICT, 'pluggable: needs only the zarr and the booster, no probmat; OOF not in-sample', is wrong on value. (1) I pulled the public CC0 booster s1_NK_ship89_plus_collision_deployed.txt (520,226 B) and parsed the text model without lightgbm. Its #1 feature is q_m_d2: 871.5 gain (12.6%), 107 splits and 29 of 300 ROOT splits. q_m_d1/q_m_d2/q_inc_d1/q_inc_d2 have trained ranges of ~1e-6 to 0.999, and the q_* plus margin_* family holds 16.5% of total gain. The booster was therefore trained WITH a linker probability matrix. (2) mito3_ship.py l.339-365 fills qmat ONLY from --probmat (a pm_src/pm_tgt/pm_prob/pm_coords npz from Corwin's own linker). The ker13 ship argv (l.148-172) passes no --probmat. Deployed, every q and margin feature is NaN, and the trees send all candidates down a NaN branch (decision_type 8/10) that was learned on the minority of rows the linker never scored. 'No probmat' is a defect, not the reason it plugs in. The +0.00063 / TP 59->61 / FP 68->70 OOF plate does not certify this regime, because it is unknown whether the plate had a probmat. Doing it properly needs a pm_* adapter from our edge probabilities, which is new code with a calibration mismatch. (3) The claimed-pool pitch is overstated. d1_is_theft, d1_is_orphan and already_kept are constant ('none') in training. The pool assumes a one-to-one linker that cannot fork (mother out-degree 1; d2 = orphan or stolen, l.366-375). The margin and q_inc features that would rank a theft are among the NaN ones. On our stack the ILP and the insertion already fork. (4) Also: import-time SystemExit self-tests and a process-wide builtins.open/Path.open monkeypatch, so the module is not fail-soft at import unless it is wrapped. The whole film goes to RAM as float32. Top-k is 1 per film (~1 edit per hidden video at 0.50 OOF precision). Old reason 'MITOSE heads not public' was wrong in name, but 'cannot plug into x138' is closer to true than the finding says: the missing piece is Corwin's linker probmat, not a head.
